download.title: A focused Japanese workspace, ready for your desktop.
download.description: Choose your platform and explore what is shipping in the YomiFlow desktop app.
download.simulated: Installer downloads will be enabled when public release builds are available.

windows.name: Windows
windows.requirements: Standard native installation. No additional YomiFlow-specific requirements.

macos.name: macOS
macos.requirementsTitle: Apple Silicon only (M1, M2, M3 and newer)
macos.requirements: Intel Macs are not supported in this release.

linux.name: Linux
linux.requirements: Your Linux distribution may ask you to install WebKitGTK if it is missing when opening the .AppImage or .deb.

requirements.title: System requirements
requirements.description: YomiFlow combines a Tauri desktop shell, Rust services and local SQLite storage. Core study data stays on your device; no hosted database is required.

local.title: Local-first core
local.description: The reader, notebook and review history use local storage. SQLite runs in WAL mode for responsive local reads and writes.

platform.title: Platform webviews
platform.description: Windows builds use WebView2; macOS uses its native WebKit webview. Linux packaging targets WebKitGTK 4.1, with distro dependencies depending on the package.

storage.title: Your library sets storage needs
storage.description: There is no published fixed memory or disk minimum yet. Imported audio, video, archives and optional OCR assets determine additional storage and compute needs.

releases.title: Recent release notes
releases.disclaimer: These are recent implementation notes from the desktop repository. The displayed installer version is a preview label; packages are not yet downloadable.

audioVault.title: Audio Vault folder import
audioVault.description: Import folders recursively, read available ID3 metadata with filename fallbacks, add tracks to the local library and optionally queue them in sorted order.

shadowingMorphman.title: More resilient study flow
shadowingMorphman.description: Shadowing now reports speech-recognition network errors clearly, and unfamiliar MorphMan terms can flow into SRS card creation.

notebook.title: Richer notebook editing
notebook.description: Notebook editing preserves HTML formatting, adds full table support and lets learners delete notes.

notebook.title: A Japanese notebook that helps you see how sentences work.
notebook.description: Write, analyze and connect study notes in a TipTap workspace with local Japanese language tools powered by Rust and Lindera.
notebook.mediaLabel: Notebook and Japanese language analysis feature video

first.title: TipTap notes with Markdown flow
first.description: Use rich-text blocks, Markdown editing, slash commands, split-screen study and autosaving to keep notes close to the material.

second.title: Lindera morphology
second.description: The Rust backend tokenizes Japanese with its bundled IPADIC dictionary and highlights parts of speech in the editor.

third.title: Bunsetsu syntax tree
third.description: Generate a dependency view that groups morphemes into Bunsetsu units and visualizes sentence relationships.

fourth.title: Grammar checks and linked notes
fourth.description: A local heuristic flags a documented particle pattern with a one-click suggestion; [[note]] links connect related notebook entries.

audioVault.title: Your listening library, always within reach.
audioVault.description: Audio Vault brings local audio, a persistent player and queue together, while OmniSearch makes your growing library easy to revisit.

first.title: A persistent global player
first.description: Playback and queue stay available as you move between study activities.

second.title: Import a local music library
second.description: Scan folders recursively and read ID3 metadata, with filename and folder fallbacks when tags are missing.

third.title: Listening history stays local
third.description: Track listened milliseconds per session in SQLite and revisit your imported audio library.

fourth.title: Search across your study data
fourth.description: Find cards, notebook notes and cached NHK articles with the SQLite FTS5 OmniSearch.

immersion.title: Read and watch Japanese with context in reach.
immersion.description: Bring manga, local video and NHK Web Easy into one reading flow, with dictionary lookups and a path from immersion to review.

first.title: Manga, without unpacking archives
first.description: Open CBZ, ZIP, CBR and RAR collections directly from memory and select speech bubbles for local MangaOCR inference with ONNX Runtime.

second.title: Video subtitles made studyable
second.description: Play local MKV and MP4 video, inspect embedded subtitles, and extract contextual audio clips and screenshots for richer flashcards with FFmpeg.

third.title: NHK Web Easy, kept nearby
third.description: Cache articles and native audio in SQLite for local reading with morphological hover breakdowns.

fourth.title: From a word to a review
fourth.description: Look up vocabulary in the media context and carry useful discoveries into your spaced-repetition decks.

shadowing.title: Listen, repeat and compare your Japanese aloud.
shadowing.description: Practice with your own audio, system-provided Japanese speech synthesis and microphone transcription when your browser supports Web Speech API.

first.title: Bring your own listening material
first.description: Load a local audio file into a focused shadowing session and replay it while practicing.

second.title: System voice playback
second.description: Ask the host browser or operating system for a ja-JP speech voice. Available voices and offline behavior depend on that platform.

third.title: Microphone transcription
third.description: The trainer requests Japanese speech recognition through Web Speech API; browser support and network requirements vary.

fourth.title: Useful feedback after a take
fourth.description: Compare recognized text with the target and get a character-level similarity score to guide another attempt.

srs.title: Review with a scheduler and a library that work together.
srs.description: YomiFlow combines FSRS and SM-2 scheduling with relational SQLite decks, review history and an interleaved study queue.

first.title: FSRS and SM-2 scheduling
first.description: Pure domain models track stability and difficulty to schedule vocabulary recall across your study decks.

second.title: Relational SQLite data
second.description: Cards connect to dictionary entries, decks, tags and review logs with foreign-key integrity and cascading cleanup.

third.title: One interleaved review queue
third.description: Mix vocabulary with image-occlusion cards, grammar notes and Kana prompts rather than staying in one exercise type.

fourth.title: Make visual details recallable
fourth.description: Mask areas of local images and reveal them during review, then schedule recall with the existing FSRS ratings.

analytics.title: Know what a passage asks of you before you dive in.
analytics.description: Use local vocabulary coverage, retention estimates and study history to understand what you know and plan what comes next.
analytics.mediaLabel: MorphMan and study analytics feature video

first.title: Offline MorphMan estimates
first.description: Lindera lemmas are compared with your SQLite vocabulary cards to estimate known-word coverage and highlight unfamiliar occurrences.

second.title: Coverage and retention, separated
second.description: See comprehension coverage alongside a distinct FSRS-based retrievability estimate for terms with cards.

third.title: JLPT coverage from N5 to N1
third.description: Compare your local dictionary and card corpus with JLPT vocabulary levels.

fourth.title: History and what is due next
fourth.description: Review GitHub-style 16-week study heatmaps and upcoming review forecasts, with completed focus sessions tracked locally.

kana.title: Build kana fluency one character at a time.
kana.description: Kana Dojo turns Hiragana and Katakana practice into short recall drills with accuracy and speed tracked per character.

first.title: Choose your character set
first.description: Practice Hiragana, Katakana or both, selecting base kana, Dakuon/Handakuon and Yoon combinations.

second.title: Fast recall drills
second.description: See a kana prompt and answer in romaji, with a new prompt ready for another focused repetition.

third.title: Character-level mastery
third.description: SQLite records attempts and correctness for each character, including accuracy and response speed.

fourth.title: Join the mixed review queue
fourth.description: Kana prompts can be interleaved with vocabulary, grammar and image-occlusion reviews.

about.title: Built with care for the long journey of learning Japanese.
about.story: YomiFlow is architected by Erick Gabriel dos Santos Alves with a simple belief: a thoughtful study tool should support curiosity, consistency and ownership. The product brings reading, listening, writing and review into one calm workspace designed to grow with each learner.
about.credentials: Its engineering reflects robust principles shaped by postgraduate studies in Software Engineering at Faculdade Descomplica, alongside a community-minded approach strengthened through selection as a Google Student Ambassador 2026.
